Although human beings have been fighting inequality and racism, and working towards justice for all, there are always more issues that arise. After the first humanitarian organization, the Red Cross, was founded in 1863, the role of humanitarians became increasingly necessary. Today, because technology and social media have advanced, the response to more recent crises such as the tsunami in Japan, the wars in Bosnia, Rwanda and Somalia, and the countless other disasters affecting people all over the world, has been huge.
Just before the world's attention was drawn to the attacks on the Twin Towers in New York City, the United Nations Global Conference on Racism was held. The conference was a step in the right direction, but the event following was not. Still, the humanitarian effort in response to the event was incredible.

Such a response was also evident when the 2010 earthquake in Haiti occurred. Doctors Without Borders have been working there since 1991 and have continued to do so on a much larger scale so that the destitute victims of the earthquake can rebuild.

The political unrest and activism in the era of The Civil Rights Movement educated people about racism and basic human rights. Unfortunately, Amnesty International has said that racism is on the rise today. The social issues have become larger with the increase in population, and though we have had good responses to disasters that occur, we still need to learn to prepare for a problem rather than only respond to it.
As humans we face varying degrees of adversity. We need to be empathetic and compassionate towards each other. It seems that we all have a role to play to ensure that people are treated with dignity, respect and equality.

You can use narrative tenses to relate events in a story.

The most common narrative tenses are the Simple Past, Past Continuous, and the Past Perfect.
You can use them in several ways and to express various relationships between past events.

Adverbial Clauses: Time, Purpose, Reason, Result, Concession - A Review
An adverbial clause is a dependent clause that acts like an adverb. With these clauses, you can express time relationships, explain a purpose or reason, present results and show concession.
